title: Risk of Foot Ulcer and Lower Extremity Amputation among Participants in the Diabetes Control and Complications Trial/Epidemiology of Diabetes Interventions and Complications Study (DCCT/EDIC)

original_source.central_claim: Early intensive glycemic control during DCCT decreases subsequent diabetic foot-ulcer risk in EDIC participants with type 1 diabetes.; Smoking predicts amputation but not ulcer risk, while continuous ankle-brachial index does not predict either outcome in the reported analysis.

central_claims: Early intensive glycemic control during DCCT decreases subsequent diabetic foot-ulcer risk in EDIC participants with type 1 diabetes.
Smoking predicts amputation but not ulcer risk, while continuous ankle-brachial index does not predict either outcome in the reported analysis.

source_manifest.title: Risk of Foot Ulcer and Lower Extremity Amputation among Participants in DCCT/EDIC (113-OR)
source_manifest.finding: Conference abstract concludes early intensive glycemic control reduces later ulcer risk; smoking and ankle-brachial index findings are also reported.

source_manifest.title: Risk of Foot Ulcer and Lower-Extremity Amputation Among Participants in DCCT/EDIC
source_manifest.finding: Same authors/cohort report reduced all-ulcer risk with intensive control; first-ulcer and amputation estimates do not reach significance. This is full-publication continuity, not independent replication.

source_manifest.title: Etiology, Epidemiology, and Disparities in the Burden of Diabetic Foot Ulcers
source_manifest.finding: Independent review cites the 2022 full report in its glycemic-management section, accepting durable ulcer-prevention benefit from early control.

source_manifest.title: Decreasing lifetime prevalence of diabetes-related foot ulcers in Norway: HUNT study
source_manifest.finding: Independent population study uses the 2022 report for risk-factor context; it does not test early randomized intensive treatment.

source_manifest.title: HbA1c and the Risk of Lower Limb Ulcers Among Diabetic Patients: An Observational and Genetics Study
source_manifest.finding: UK Biobank study finds an observational glycemia–ulcer association but nonsignificant genetic causal estimates; its broader lower-limb outcome and mostly type-2 sample do not reproduce the DCCT early-treatment claim.

source_manifest.title: Evaluating and mapping the evidence that screening for diabetic foot disease meets population-wide screening criteria
source_manifest.finding: Scoping review cites the full report for ulcer/amputation background, not a test of its intervention effect.

answers.rationale: The full 2022 report is from the original team. HUNT and UK Biobank do not explicitly test early intensive treatment in type 1 diabetes; independent primary support of that exact claim remains unverified.
No independent trial or cohort reconstruction reproduced the early randomized-treatment legacy effect.
The 2022 report adds full analyses, but accessible records did not establish that it is a larger or stricter test than the 2018 abstract.
An independent clinical synthesis retains the early-control ulcer-prevention conclusion through the 2022 full report of the same study.

evidence.explanation: Glycemic Management section explicitly accepts a lasting early-control benefit and cites the matched full report.

answers.rationale: No read follow-up directly tests the original ascertainment or confounding limitations and demonstrates robustness of the early-treatment effect.
Later studies address glycemia and ulcer risk, but an extension specifically built on this early-treatment result was not established.
Independent groups cite the full article, but two substantive extensions of this particular contribution were not established.
Later studies employ standard epidemiological methods; reuse of an original method or result as an analytic input was not verified.
The review credits the finding as evidence, without identifying it as the origin of a research direction.
The independent primary studies do not use the original early-treatment estimate as a numerical benchmark or reference construction.
A preventive implication is accepted, but no independently measured clinical benefit attributable to applying this particular finding was verified.
The later glycemia–ulcer associations do not demonstrate successful application of the early-treatment finding outside DCCT/EDIC.
The later full report gives more detail, but a genuinely new result enabled by the abstract itself was not established.
Intensive glycemic control was established practice before this abstract; no new workflow adoption attributable to this foot-ulcer result was verified.
No independent fair treatment comparison directly establishes the claimed ulcer-risk reduction; the matched full report is the same cohort.
The original finding, carried into its full report, is substantively used in a prevention synthesis after three years.

evidence.explanation: The finding informs clinical interpretation in the 2022-online/2023-print review.

answers.rationale: The independent review positively assesses the early-treatment finding more than four years after the 2018 abstract.

evidence.explanation: Published December 2022, the review uses the full report to support early glucose management.

answers.rationale: The 2022 synthesis is substantive; later primary citations do not establish substantive building on the specific early-treatment result in another year.
The matched full publication is incorporated into an independent clinical research synthesis as useful prevention evidence.

evidence.explanation: The review incorporates the result into its glycemic-management interpretation.

answers.rationale: The review endorses prevention implications but does not explicitly compare their continued usefulness against newer approaches.

search_gaps: Original is a conference abstract, not a full article; no presentation or complete original numerical table was retrieved.

The 2022 article is mapped as the likely full publication from matching title, authors, cohort and conclusion; its abstract was read because full-text requests failed. It is not counted as independent.
Independent observational glycemia evidence is distinguished from randomized early-treatment evidence; nonsignificant genetic estimates are not treated as refutation.
Lifetime observation through 2026-09-16; the assigned pilot sample is not an unbiased estimate of all research outcomes.
research.summary: The conference finding persisted into a same-team full report and an independent prevention synthesis. Independent replication and practical effects attributable to this specific result remain unverified.
